coverage: Read all 25 criteria and both assignments' prompts for sequence. Read the supplied facts and pertinent portions of the attached Iowa statutes and cases, including Ellison, Kehoe, Poe, and White Horse; independently read relevant 2020 Iowa Code sections from the legislature. The Patton State Plea text extract contained only stamps, so I downloaded the pinned PDF and visually read all six scanned pages: count VIII concerns the May 10 conspiracy, while count XX concerns April 13 intimidation. The separate official Eighth Circuit opinion was read to check law, not treated as a permitted source for the assigned brief. No solver call was made.

findings.title: Conspiracy alone does not trigger the forcible-felony bar
findings.explanation: The criterion awards a categorical assertion that commission of conspiracy to commit a forcible felony precludes justification. Iowa Code section 704.6(1) instead bars a person participating in a forcible felony; section 702.11 does not enumerate conspiracy, and sections 706.1 and 706.4 treat conspiracy as a separate offense that can be established without completion of the planned felony. The scanned plea confirms Patton admitted planning a May 10 shooting, but does not convert that admission into commission of an enumerated forcible felony. A careful prosecutor could argue Patton participated in an actual felonious assault on the facts, but should not say that the conspiracy offense itself automatically forecloses the defense. The criterion therefore rewards an incorrect shortcut and fails a legally precise brief.

evidence.quote: States that Patton's commission of conspiracy to commit a forcible felony precludes a justification defense.
One who is participating in a forcible felony, or riot, or a duel.
Agrees with another that they or one or more of them will engage in conduct constituting the crime or an attempt or solicitation to commit the crime.

authorities.proposition: The statutory bar applies to one participating in a forcible felony.
The enumerated forcible felonies do not include conspiracy as a separate offense.
Conspiracy is established by agreement and an overt act, and is a separate offense from any public offense committed pursuant to the agreement.

findings.suggested_fix: Credit a supported argument that Patton participated in an actual enumerated forcible felony, or an accurately qualified argument about how the conspiracy admission bears on intent; do not require the proposition that conspiracy itself invokes section 704.6(1).

findings.title: Penalty for accurately mentioning a separate intimidation plea
findings.explanation: Penalty misfire: the scanned plea has two separate counts. Patton pleaded guilty to intimidation with a dangerous weapon for discharging a gun into an occupied vehicle on April 13, 2020; he separately pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit a forcible felony based on a planned May 10 shooting. The negative criterion deducts for any mention that Patton pleaded guilty to intimidation, even if a careful prosecutor correctly dates and distinguishes that earlier offense and says it does not prove a May 10 intimidation offense or bar self-defense. The adjacent penalties for claiming May 10 intimidation are narrower and defensible. Criterion_23, as written, fails an accurate distinction of the two plea counts.

evidence.quote: Mentions that Patton pled guilty in state court to intimidation with a dangerous weapon.
On or about April 13, 2020, in Polk County, Iowa, I did discharging a gun into the vehicle of another person
On or about May 10, 2020, in Polk County, Iowa, I did conspire with other individuals to commit a forcible felony

findings.suggested_fix: Penalize misdating the intimidation plea or relying on it as proof that Patton committed intimidation on May 10; allow accurate mention of the separate April 13 plea.
